entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv5315"/><title type="x-s2">CHAPTER 38</title> <div sID="gen7966" type="x-p"/> <reference osisRef="Job.38.1-Job.38.41">Job 38:1-41</reference>.<div eID="gen7966" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen7967" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv5315"/>1. Jehovah appears unexpectedly in a whirlwind (already gathering <reference osisRef="Job.37.1">Job 37:1</reference>, 2), the symbol of "judgment" (<reference osisRef="Ps.50.3">Psa 50:3</reference>, <reference osisRef="Ps.50.4">4</reference>, &c.), to which Job had challenged Him. He asks him now to get himself ready for the contest. Can he explain the phenomena of God's natural government? How can he, then, hope to understand the principles of His moral government? God thus confirms Elihu's sentiment, that submission to, not reasonings on, God's ways is man's part. This and the disciplinary design of trial to the godly is the great lesson of this book. He does not solve the difficulty by reference to future retribution: for this was not the immediate question; glimpses of that truth were already given in the fourteenth and nineteenth chapters, the full revelation of it being reserved for Gospel times. Yet even now we need to learn the lesson taught by Elihu and God in Job. <div eID="gen7967" type="x-p"/>

So at the founding of Zerubbabel's temple (<reference osisRef="Ezra.3.10-Ezra.3.13">Ezr 3:10-13</reference>). So hereafter at the completion of the Church, the temple of the Holy Ghost (<reference osisRef="Zech.4.7">Zec 4:7</reference>); as at its foundation (<reference osisRef="Luke.2.13">Lu 2:13</reference>, <reference osisRef="2Cor.2.14">14</reference>).<div eID="gen7978" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen7979" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">morning stars--</hi>especially beautiful. The creation morn is appropriately associated with these, it being the commencement of this world's day. The stars are figuratively said to sing God's praises, as in <reference osisRef="Ps.19.1">Psa 19:1</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ps.148.3">148:3</reference>. They are symbols of the angels, bearing the same relation to our earth, as angels do to us. Therefore they answer to "sons of God," or angels, in the parallel. See on <reference osisRef="Job.25.5">Job 25:5</reference>. <div eID="gen7979" type="x-p"/>
